question: What is the formula unit mass of sodium chloride (NaCl)?
solution: The correct answer is __**58.5u**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **formula unit mass** of a substance is the sum of the **atomic masses** of all atoms in a formula unit of a compound. • For compounds that consist of **ions** (ionic compounds), the term **formula unit mass** is used instead of **molecular mass** because these substances do not consist of discrete molecules. • **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)** is a classic example of an **ionic compound**. It consists of **Sodium (Na+)** cations and **Chloride (Cl-)** anions arranged in a crystal lattice. • The **atomic mass** of **Sodium (Na)** is **23 u**. • The **atomic mass** of **Chlorine (Cl)** is **35.5 u**. • The **formula unit mass** of **NaCl** is calculated as: **1 × 23 u + 1 × 35.5 u = 58.5 u**. • ***Hence, the correct answer is 58.5u.***
